text:
marc: Quick heads-up — did a region-by-region placement + commitment binpack sketch for inference clusters. Short version: mixing us-central + eu-west committed capacity and keeping apac mostly on-demand looks like the best cost/latency tradeoff under current traffic.
anya: can you drop the numbers? interested in egress impact too.
marc: sure. main assumptions: 1) baseline q2 traffic shape, 2) 40% reserved GPU commit (1yr), 3) spot available for burst. rough outputs below.
marc: Cost sketch (monthly):
- us-central: GPU unit price committed ~ $1.78/hr -> effective $1.20/hr after commit amortization; expected usage 55% -> monthly est $145k
- eu-west: GPU unit committed ~ $1.95/hr -> effective $1.30/hr; expected usage 30% -> monthly est $80k
- apac (sin): on-demand/spot mix -> weighted avg $2.30/hr; expected usage 15% -> monthly est $60k
- cross-region egress: ~ $12k/mo if we serve cached prefixes cross-region; local routing reduces to ~$4k/mo
marc: Overall monthly spend ~ $285k with commitments vs ~ $345k pure on-demand (~17.4% savings).

derek: where did the egress numbers come from? did you include model shard syncs/kv-cache refreshes?
marc: yes, small refreshes every 6h per pod, and a worst-case model sync during deploys counted as one-time spike. the steady-state egress var is mostly prefix cache misses; that 12k is if we actively route 30% cross-region.
sanjay: latency SLOs for apac customers — are they okay with being routed to apac on-demand nodes?
marc: measured p50/p95 if routed: apac->sin on-demand p95 ~ 140ms for typical LLMs; apac->eu p95 is ~220ms so not acceptable. so we keep dedicated on-demand pools in apac for low-latency buckets and fall back to eu/us only for non-SLO traffic.
anya: what about commitment risk? if traffic drops we get locked into reserved cost.
derek: can we do convertible or regional-flex commitments to mitigate? some clouds allow more flexible commitments.
marc: looked into that — convertible reduces discount a bit but gives us reallocation flexibility. proposal: commit 40% in us-central, 30% eu-west, 0% apac initially. Keep a 3-month review window and convertible reservation for 20% of the commit to enable reallocation.
marc: quick commands used (billing query):
```sql
SELECT region, SUM(cost) as cost, SUM(egress_bytes)/1024/1024/1024 as egress_gb
FROM billing WHERE service = 'compute' AND month = '2025-02' GROUP BY region;
```
marc: and a small python sketch for binpacking expected GPU-hours: 
```py
def pack(commit_hours, demand_hours):
    # naive binpack: commit where demand > threshold
    return sum(min(c,d) for c,d in zip(commit_hours, demand_hours))
```

sanjay: +1 to a phased approach. can we keep a small buffer reserved in apac (say 5%) to reduce cold-start pain for bursts?
anya: 5% sounds reasonable as safety. also request: add a sensitivity column for 10/20/30% traffic drop so finance can model downside.
marc: will add sensitivity models. initial ask to leadership: approve 40/30/25/5 (us/eur/apac/convertible) split and start 1yr commitments with convertible flags on 20% of total.
derek: any impact on placement logic or autoscaler? need to ensure autoscaler prefers reserved pools for steady traffic and keeps spot for burst.
marc: yep, scheduler change: annotate routes with "prefer_reserved":true for steady routes; autoscaler will prefer reserved-backed node pools. I'll open a PR with the scheduler tweak after approvals.
anya: sounds good. @derek @sanjay please ack if you can live with the 1yr convertible plan and the 3-month review cadence. :thumbsup:
derek: ack
sanjay: ack
ops-bot: Note: deployment window for reserved purchase will be 2025-03-01 02:00 UTC -> rolling provisioning.
marc: thanks — I'll produce the sensitivity spreadsheet and the PR for autoscaler changes. meeting to finalize on Monday.
